proposals.impact: lift 37.5% open rate closer to the 66% vigilance benchmark
proposals.observation: The Money Worship automation has a 37.5% open rate (6 opens from 16 sends). The Money Vigilance automation is running at 66.67% on a similar send volume (12 sends). Both sequences target earners who completed the same quiz, so the audience quality is comparable. The most controllable variable separating a 37% open rate from a 67% one at low send volumes is the subject line. A single subject-line rewrite on email 1 of the Money Worship sequence is a one-file, low-risk change that could close a meaningful portion of that gap within the next send cycle.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the subject line of email 1 in the Money Worship automation. The current subject line is not available in the data, so the replacement below is written on the assumption it uses a category label or a benefit promise ("Your money type is Money Worship", "Here's what that means for you", or similar). Category-label subjects perform poorly because they complete the reader's curiosity before the email is opened. The replacement below uses a specific, lived detail that speaks to the Money Worship pattern without naming the category, so the reader's recognition does the work.

---
title: "The bonus cleared on a Friday. By Sunday it was gone. Why does that keep happening?"
pubDate: 2026-06-30
description: "Spending the moment money arrives is not a willpower failure. It is a pattern with a name, and it is worth looking at honestly."
tags: [money-worship, behavioural-patterns, spending]
---

The notification came through at 11am on a Friday.
The bonus, the one you had been watching the calendar for since January, landed.

By Sunday evening you had a new laptop, two rounds of dinner for friends you had been meaning to catch up with, and a gym membership you felt genuinely good about.

By Tuesday the account was back to where it usually sits.

You were not reckless. You did not buy anything you regret.
But somehow the number is the same as it was before the bonus existed.

This is not a story about discipline.
It is about what money means to the part of your brain that runs the show before you have time to think.

For some people, money sitting unspent feels genuinely uncomfortable. Not lazy, not irresponsible. Uncomfortable in a specific, physical way, the way a task on a to-do list itches until you tick it off. The moment money arrives, the urge to move it somewhere, spend it, give it, use it, is stronger than most planning advice accounts for.

Behavioural economists call this pattern Money Worship. The name sounds dramatic. The experience usually does not feel dramatic at all. It feels like living, like generosity, like finally doing the thing you wanted to do. The consequence only shows up later, quietly, when you check the balance and the number has not moved in the direction you expected.

Joel Larkin, MSc Behavioural Economics | Qualified Financial Planner, works with earners in their 20s and 30s who are good at making money and find that the building part keeps not happening. If this post felt like it was written about you, the [money psychology quiz](/quiz) takes four minutes and tells you something specific about your own pattern.
